text: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run swiftly and be glorified, just as it is among you,

versions.text: Finally, brothers, pray for us, that the word of the Lord may run its course and be honored, just as it was among you,
versions.explanation: The verb is elided in Greek and the comparison is with the present situation in Thessalonica, so "is" fits better than "was." Also, δοξάζηται is the standard "glorified" language of praise for God's word; "honored" weakens it slightly.

text: and that we may be rescued from perverse and evil people — for not everyone has faith.
But the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.
And we are confident in the Lord about you, that you are doing and will go on doing what we command.
May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the steadfastness of Christ.
Now we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, to keep away from every brother who lives an undisciplined life and not according to the tradition they received from us.
For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us: we were not idle when we were with you,
nor did we eat anyone's bread without paying for it. Instead, we worked night and day, laboring and struggling, so that we would not be a burden to any of you.
Not that we lack the right to such support, but we wanted to give you an example to imitate.
For even when we were with you, we gave you this command: if anyone is unwilling to work, he should not eat.
We hear that some among you are living undisciplined lives, doing no work at all but meddling in the work of others.

versions.text: We hear that some among you are living undisciplined lives, not busy working but busybodies.
versions.explanation: "Not busy working but busybodies" reads awkwardly aloud and blurs the sense of μηδὲν ἐργαζομένους (doing no work). The suggested wording keeps the Greek wordplay's contrast while flowing better for oral reading.

text: Such people we command and urge in the Lord Jesus Christ to work quietly and eat their own bread.

versions.text: Such people we command and urge in the Lord Jesus Christ to settle down, work quietly, and eat their own bread.
versions.explanation: "Settle down" is an added third element not present in the Greek, which has only two ideas: working quietly (μετὰ ἡσυχίας ἐργαζόμενοι) and eating their own bread. Removing it keeps the verse faithful and tightens the rhythm.

text: As for you, brothers, do not grow weary of doing good.
If anyone does not obey what we say in this letter, take note of him. Have nothing to do with him, so that he may be ashamed.
Yet do not regard him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.
Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace at all times and in every way. The Lord be with you all.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. This is the mark of every letter of mine; this is how I write.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all.
